body:
Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/390
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

`corvint impact` and the `corvint_impact` MCP tool accept only `.go` paths; the MCP input schema enforces a `.go` suffix. Repositories whose product code is Ruby, JavaScript, or TypeScript cannot get revision-bound impact evidence for a change. Flow documentation (`docs flows generate`) already recognizes several constructs in those languages: Ruby methods and jobs, literal Rails routes, JS/TS functions, and Angular registrations.

## Requested capability

- Range impact (`impact --base`) and path impact for the languages that already have analyzers (at least Ruby, JavaScript, and TypeScript), with the same receipt shape and explicit `unknown` entries for dynamic dispatch.
- A per-language capability table in `impact --help` and in the MCP tool description, so callers know what is covered.

## Acceptance

- Conformance fixtures for each added language, including negative cases where dispatch is dynamic.
- The MCP schema admits the new suffixes.
- Unsupported constructs appear as unknowns, not as absence.

## Why

A post-merge documentation and test workflow (see the umbrella) needs impact evidence for the language the product is written in. Otherwise the whole loop has to fall back to external providers for its most basic question.


Part of #388.
title: GH #390: Feature: range and path impact for non-Go languages (impact accepts only .go today)
